inlines.v: PAIR, noun [Latin par; Heb. to join, couple or associate.] 1. Two things of a kind, similar in form, applied to the same purpose, and suited to each other or used together; as a pair of gloves or stockings; a pair of shoes; a pair of oxen or horses. 2. Two of a sort; a couple; a brace; as a pair of nerves; a pair of doves. Luke 2:24. PAIR, verb intransitive To be joined in pairs; to couple, as, birds pair in summer. 1. To suit; to fit; as a counterpart. Ethelinda, My heart was made to fit and pair with thine. PAIR, verb transitive To unite in couples; as minds paired in heaven. 1. To unite as correspondent, or rather to contrast. Glossy jet is paired with shining white. PAIR, verb transitive To impair. [See Impair.]
